segments.text: section 1.3 approaches. Common activities in bioinformatics include mapping and analyzing DNA
and protein sequences, aligning different DNA and protein sequences to compare them,
and creating and viewing 3D models of protein structures. There are two fundamental ways of
modeling a biological system, i.e. a living cell, both coming under bioinformatic approaches.
1. Static Sequences Proteins, nucleic acids and peptides
Interaction data among the above entities including microarray data and networks of proteins
and metabolites. 2. Dynamic Structures Proteins, nucleic acids, ligands,
including metabolites and drugs and peptides. Structures studied with bioinformatics tools
are not considered static anymore, and their dynamics is often the core of these structural studies.
